Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min

text_fidelity_a:
NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

I'm not usually very impressed with toy vehicles because I have seen so many of them and because most of them look very similar. But this toy vehicle grabbed my attention. The cool, eye- catching, all- around design pattern is one that is bound to warrant a second look and both adults and kids alike will find that it easily stands out against other toy vehicles.

Aside from the exterior, this Monster High vehicle does have other features that make it cool. The stylish wheels glide smoothly across a tile floor or a table without any problem and the vehicle seats up to four Monster High dolls. Rather than have all four dolls face forward, this convertible is a two- seat model with a pair of seats that are actually on top of the trunk, where the dolls face backward. Again, it's something unique that you don't find with other toy vehicles.

The Monster High Travel Scaris Vehicle doesn't have any lights or sounds. This may bother some youngsters, but it is better from an adult perspective because it means no batteries to buy and more imagination required. Most kids will not mind anyway- they will find the vehicle so cool and fun that they will not even notice that it doesn't make noise or have any lights. And another advantage is that boys and girls both seem to like this toy. Girls like it because its Monster High and boys like it because, well, it's a vehicle, which is a toy normally associated with boys.

This Monster High vehicle doesn't have opening side doors, and this is one quality that I wish was different because it would not only look cool, but it would also make it easier to place the dolls into the seats. But other than that, this is a fun, nice- looking toy that belongs in the home of every Monster High fan.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle

Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up Chess has been my favorite board game since I was a child and I have collected chess sets as a hobby over the years. When I selected this one I expected it to be on par with typical portable wooden sets which are usually cheaply made. This one was a pleasant surprise in that it is a step up from most portable wooden sets I have seen and used.

This is a fairly straightforward set. The case is a clamshell design that folds open into the board. There are magnets in the rim of the underside of the board to hold it closed when the set is not in use, ands the manufacturer did a decent job of concealing the contacts (though they are visible if you look for them). The squares on the board are smooth and while the seams between the squares can be felt when you run your hand along the board, the seams are smooth and are less pronounced that what I have seen on some other boards.

The pieces are decently made though are nothing special. They are machine cut pieces and have been smoothed, sanded and varnished. They are weighted nicely and have felt on the bottom to avoid scratching the board. They’re a fairly average design but they look good and are very recognizable.

The main feature of this set is that it is larger than most fold-out boards I have seen and used. While this might not be the best for packing and portability, I really like the size. I am less likely to knock over pieces accidentally and I can see what’s going on a little better.

This is not just a chess set but includes wood chips for playing checkers as well. The chips are small and are nothing of note but they are sufficient.

I really like this chess set and will use it as my main travel set moving forward. I like the size of the board, the feel of the pieces and the overall quality. There are better sets out there but they cost more. There are less expensive sets too, and the chances of finding one that is of the same quality as this one for less is small.
text_fidelity_b: Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up

Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit This THAMES & KOSMOS THE BIG ENGINEERING MAKERSPACE SCIENCE EXPERIMENT KIT is the real deal--a fun model-building kit that painlessly teaches basic concepts of physics (e.g., thermal air currents, levers, momentum). Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.

K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy [[VIDEOID:5795137e2a23bd3d76a56d2b9446c889]] If you’re already familiar with K’Nex building sets, this K’NEX THRILL RIDES-REVOLUTION FERRIS WHEEL is a simple, fast build. The Ferris wheel is big, but it doesn’t require a lot of pieces. Also, much of the assembly involves building duplicate parts that combine to make the wheel and its swinging gondolas.

The set is recommended for age 7+, and that sounds reasonable (assuming that an adult provides some initial help with making the connections, and assists with lifting the wheel onto the axle). Each shape of piece is a different color, which detracts from the appearance of the finished Ferris wheel, but makes the construction simpler. There aren’t many “snowflake” connections, which I usually have to puzzle over to get the right orientation. (K’Nex pieces are much harder to work with than LEGO pieces.) The instructions are reasonably clear. This set took me about 5 hours to build (from opening the box to completion, working at a leisurely pace).

Unfortunately, the finished “thrill ride” isn’t very thrilling. Like a full-sized amusement park ride, the Ferris wheel doesn’t do much—it just goes around and around in a circle. Also, it does NOT have a variable speed control—you cannot start, stop, or speed up the wheel gradually (like a real ride). Although the motor has a single speed, it does run in forward and reverse directions. The motor is powered by two AA batteries (not included).

For the Ferris wheel to turn properly, one edge of the inner wheel track must be settled into the groove on the “gear wheel” attached to the motor. You can easily fiddle with the base to adjust things so that the track and groove always make good contact. Because it’s sort of boring and lacks a variable speed control, I rate this K’Nex Ferris Wheel kit at 4 stars (“I like it” on the official Amazon scale).
text_fidelity_b: K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy

Hot Wheels T-Rex Rampage Track Set, Works City Sets, Toys for Boys Ages 5 to 10 My son has several sets of Hot Wheels toys. Hot Wheels is often hit or miss. They sometimes have a great idea and an awesomely executed toy. Sometimes the toys create nothing but frustration. However, with this playset my really had nothing but fear. Therefore, the Mattel Hot Wheels City T-Rex Rampage has done it's job. It strikes fear in all those who come upon it. My 7 year old is afraid of this toy. He was ok with it until he found out that the T-Rex moved, and it's no dice. He doesn't even want it just sitting in his room.

After you figure out how to put it together. The T-Rex part was tricky, but don't worry the part can come apart so if you mess up the alignment, you're ok. You get 1 angry T-Rex who needs a snack and a nap, 2 buildings, a launchpad, and a piece of track and a car. I'm not sure what the name of the game is. I am not entirely sure what you are supposed to do. My son comes up with different ideas every 5 minutes. However, the scary part comes in when you turn it on. The toy comes with batteries and when you turn it on and push the blue button on the circle track, the T-Rex will start to thrash around and knock over buildings etc. He roars and all of this action is what scares my son. The launcher is of course his favorite part. If you launch the car just right, the car will hit a button to "defeat" the dinosaur.

The ultimate issue with Hot Wheels is that except for the cars themselves, most sets get broken fairly quickly. I cannot say the same for this because it's not getting much play. As with all Hot Wheel sets you can connect them to each other if you have enough track to do so. So, that is the best part about Hot Wheels. However, tracks are hard to come by and they are usually long and flimsy. So, you can't really link up the sets and the tracks get all bent out of shape. So, this will connect to the other sets we have. However, that is only great thing about it. I don't really get the whole dinosaurs or mutant alligators are taking over the city. Neither does my son. I'm all for imagination, but this whole concept seems to have been created in a vacuum. There is no background story, nothing. My son asked why is the T-Rex in the city. I had nothing.

Predators Top Trumps Card Game This card game is played in the United Kingdom. It isn't difficult to play. This is how you play:
2-6 Players
30 Predator cards including the Great White Shark, the Lion, Leopard and the American Alligator
Learn about the world's most dangerous Predators from the Great White Shark to the Lion
Simple to play - difficult to master!
1. Shuffle and deal the cards face down.
2. Players pick up their cards and look at their top cards only.
3. Player 1 (left of dealer) chooses and calls out their best stat (e.g. 'Speed - 20').
4. The other players see if they can beat this stat (Highest number wins).
5. The card with the highest stat wins all of the top cards and adds them to the base of their pile.
6. The winner of the round chooses the stat for the next round.
7. The first player to get all of the cards wins!
The game is recommended for ages 6 an up. Each card gives information about the predator. The company makes a number of card decks for different subjects.

Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up Kinetic sand is a fun activity for young kids, like regular sand it has tendency to get all over the place if not contained in a tray or plastic dish but it is easy to clean up and unlike play-doh and other similar modeling toys it doesn't ever dry out. This bake shop set comes with a roller and variety of stamps and molds to make cookies and cupcakes which are all nice quality. I especially like that the molds can fit within the roller for easy storage.

The only downside to this set is that kinetic sand is not really ideal for molding since it has a tendency to flow and collapse if not packed very tightly. Our 5 year old was trying to reproduce some of the cupcake designs shown on the box and was getting frustrated because the sand kept falling apart when she added the icing on top of the cupcake base. I tried to do it myself and was able to reproduce the design but it required packing the sand very tightly and then being very delicate when removing from the molds..

We like kinetic sand, and we like the molds that come with this set but we will probably use them primarily with play-doh instead of kinetic sand because these small molds are kind of difficult for kids to use with kinetic sand. We have some other larger ice cream molds that we have used with kinetic sand in the past, they are easier to use because they are smoother and release the sand without requiring such a delicate touch to prevent it crumbling.
text_fidelity_b: Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Short version of the review: it’s a fun game with a pretty good first-game learning curve that settles in pretty quickly in subsequent games. It can be long (though you can adjust it). We’ll add it to our rotation of “lengthy” games

Longer version

1) Packing
I’m going to ding the game for packaging because while everything comes fine (as is typical, there’s a lot of popping pieces out of their cardboard sheets), I like when games include easy ways of keeping thing together and/or organized once you’ve played the first game. Even if it’s as minimal as separate small plastic bags. We used our own tiny bags (we’ve learned to keep ones that do come with other games if they’re extra thanks to consolidation) and a few regular small baggies, but I don’t think it’s too much to ask that those things be included

2) Materials
All the materials seem of good quality. Cards are not super-thick but they’re not at all flimsy, the non-plastic pieces feel solid and you don’t have any sense that they’ll start coming apart or getting dented/torn. The plastic cities are a nice touch, but the capital cities could perhaps have been made a little more distinctive. Not at all a big deal; a close look is all you need.

3) Instructions
The big sheet of instructions is fine. Generally clear and well written, with a few “clarification” points at the end, which is a nice touch. We had a few questions that weren’t included, but they were easy to find online. A few individual player cards with a stripped down bit of instruction for quick, easy reference would have been nice to toss in

4) Set up
As noted (and as is usual for these types of games) there’s a lot of popping things out and organizing. Once that’s done the first time, set-up is relatively quick. You put together some map tiles which is easy enough (though this 50+-year-old wouldn’t have minded if the organizing numbers were a little bigger on each tile). Each player gets tokens, a set of cards five of which are laid out in a particular order under their “Focus” bar (the cards are in these areas: Military, Technology, Culture, Economy, Industry), a set of “diplomacy” cards, a “leader” card (who they “play”—Cleopatra for instance), a few caravans (little wagons used for trading). After you’ve done it a few times it’s a pretty quick set-up. You also set up some cards to the side of the play area (World Wonder cards and City-State Diplomacy Cards and Victory Cards (these are what determine how the game is won). This is always an issue in these sorts of game because of course they’re not going to be truly “visible” to all the players. Someone is going to have to move or ask to see them to see what they say (some change throughout the game). I have no idea how to get around that though; it’s just a matter of physical setting.

5) game play
I’m not going to detail it. But generally, the Victory cards have two “agendas” on them, such as build two Wonders of the World, and a player who achieves one agenda from each of the cards is the winner (this is nice because you can shorten the game if desired by simply playing with fewer Victory cards). As far as the play itself
1) Players can “resolve” (do what it says) any one of the five cards below their Focus bar. This might mean building a city, attacking someone, moving a caravan, laying out a “Control” piece to claim a hex space (i.e. territory).
2) Once they’ve done that, that card gets move to slot one under the bar and all the others move one slot to the right. This is key because the slot number affects how the card is resolved. For instance, when you attack using your military card, you roll a die and add the slot number (and possibly other bonuses) to your roll. So you’re going to want to attack when that card is in the 4 or 5 position typically, not the 1 or 2 slot. This adds a nice bit of complexity to your action choices.

That’s pretty much the gameplay for players. A few other factor include
1) You can swap out a card under your focus by advancing your “Tech” counter a certain number (you do that using one of the cards). Once you hit a certain level, you can exchange one low level card for one that’s a bit more powerful. There are 4 levels of cards.
2) Barbarian tokens on the board move at regular periods and they can end up destroying one of your caravans or claiming territory from you (which affects how much money your cities earn and how much you can advance)
3) Caravans allow you to gain trade tokens that can be used to increase the impact of your cards. For example, if you have two trade tokens on your military card, you can spend one or both to add a bonus to your roll. Caravans can also garner you another player’s Diplomacy card, which has certain benefits dependent on the card.
4) Placing a control tokens mean you’ve claimed territory (that particular space), which is necessary for collecting trade tokens (a “mature” city garners you a set number of trade tokens once you’ve “controlled” all adjacent tiles), collecting resources such as marble or diamonds, or for building cities (your build cities a certain number of spaces from a space you’ve controlled with a token).
5) The terrain has an impact on your choices. In order of scaled “easiness”, the terrains are 1-grasslands, 2-hills, 3-forest, 4-desert, and 5-mountains. To travel through a desert is considered difficult, so that 4 means your Economy card (the one that moves your caravan) needs to be in the 4 or 5 slot. Similary, to build a city in a mountain space means your Industry card has to be in the 5 slot.

There are more rules and factors that come into play, but that’s the general gist. As noted at the start, I’d say the learning curve is relatively steep the first time ( a lot of going back to the instruction booklet), but past the first game or two, it comes pretty easily. I’ve certainly played games with a far steeper curve and one that takes longer to get to know game play well. If I were ranking learning curves on a ten-point scale, I’d probably put this around a 6.

Turns move slowly the first time or two as people try to remember what they can do, what they need to do, etc. But after the first hour each player moves pretty quickly through their turns as you’ve gotten used to how to deal with the complexities of those shifting slots under the Focus bar. As people get closer to each other, things slow again as players try and figure out cost-benefit of attacking, but then as before, after a few attacks those move quickly.

I liked the game quite a bit. More than my two family members, but I tend to have more patience for the slowness of things and I mind long game less than they do. They did like it enough to play again. And as mentioned, I like that you can self-adjust your length simply by cutting out one of the agendas. It’s a game we’ll definitely keep and keep playing.
text_fidelity_b: Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces) This is a great quality play set with hundreds of pieces that will keep your kids occupied for hours. The box says 569 pieces, which is enough to build a lot of different objects.

As a parent, it's not hard to see the advantage of Lego sets. Although I think it's a little ridiculous to assume that your kid will grow up to be an engineer if they play with Legos, it's easy to see the benefit of a toy that makes children follow rigorous and complex instructions.

The build diagrams are a lot like you will encounter on any number of products in your lifetime, for everything from maintaining your vacuum cleaner, to the owner's manual of your vehicle, to how to put on a compression valve. The early you learn how to sit down and interpret an instructional diagram, the better equipped you are to deal with life.

The most amazing thing about Lego sets is that even though they are a rigorous mental exercise, kids love digging into them each and every time. This set is triple the fun as it contains the instructions for three different builds. My kids are 7 and 9 and they put together the boat in a couple hours. The boat even has a mechanism that allows you to spin a handle on the top and it makes the propeller spin (although we couldn't quite get the piece to set in place properly). Still, this is a complex build that gives a little bit of insight into gearing.

The best part is, once they're done building all the suggestions, they break the whole thing down and start constructing fortresses and whatnot. I have never seen a kid disappointed to receive a Lego set ever. Great toy.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces)

BIBIELF Bat Decor I cannot begin to tell you how much fun our entire family is having with this robot! (Well, almost the entire family...the cats hate it but the dog LOVES it!) I am truly impressed as to how well this toy works and all of the features it includes. I usually mention at the end of a review my opinion as to whether an item is worth the price but I feel the need to start with that in this review. I cannot believe how low the price of Rock Robot is. I would expected it to cost FAR more than it does!

Other than needing place 2 AA batteries (NOT included) in the controller, there is no assembly required. The robot has an on/off button on the front and rather than using batteries, it is charged using a USB cord (included). Charging does take a few hours but then Rock takes off, moves, dances, sings, plays, etc for a good 30-45 minutes straight before needing to be charged again.

As soon as its turned on, Rock giggles and introduces himself. He lights up as well. The remote controller has a SO many different functions and works well. We have experienced a few times when we had to turn the robot off and back on again after using a lot of the controller functions in a short time. (The robot will stay lit but not perform the controller functions. Its truly NOT a big deal. Turning off and back on again is all it takes and he's back in action) Rock can walk or slide; frontwards or backwards, fast/slow-pretty much whatever you want him to do. If he's gliding and comes to a stop, he doesn't tip over! I keep thinking he's going to tip but he has not fallen over even one time! He dances, sings and even moonwalks. He has a bunch of stories to tell as well with the simple press of a button. The volume as well as the voice is easily controlled with the controller.

The gesture sensing function is pretty neat. A simple command using your hand will make Rock move backward or forward/left or right.

Rock appears to be well-made. As mentioned, he hasn't fallen over once. It glides/walks/dances, etc VERY easily on flooring. (Rock does not work well on thick carpet) The controller is easy to use as well. I feel the need to mention my husband has a hearing impairment and cannot always understand what the robot is saying-he has trouble making out the words. However, the rest of us can understand it perfectly fine.

We truly are having a blast playing with this robot. I cannot recommend it enough. Its fun and entertaining and WOW, is the price ever incredibly LOW!
text_fidelity_b: BIBIELF Bat Decor

Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz. One of our kids has been on a slime kick of late, so we got this glue to add some dimension to the experience.

WHAT IS THIS GLUE LIKE?
This glue is a bit different on the label from the other color changing glue that we have used. It states that as you play, it will change in color from darker to lighter green. There is no odor and it is pretty standard type glue.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM WITH SLIME?
We used this with the Elmer's slime maker solution and got a nice slime. It makes a good consistency, and the slime is fun to play with if it is mixed at the right ratio.

DOES IT CHANGE COLOR?
That is where we have some issues. Perhaps because it is winter where we are testing this, but the slime does not want to change color unless it is really warm, something that only happens in sunlight after a while. Perhaps when it is warmer weather, or a really well heated room this will change more easily. For now, to get it to change to light green, we have to make it get REALLY warm in the sunlight in the window for a while.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a pretty green slime. It will change color if it gets really warm, but not as easily as we expected.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This does not change color that easily, so for that I have removed 1 star. It is still fun to play with as green slime, with the added bonus of changing color once in a great while when the conditions are just right, an added bonus.
text_fidelity_b: Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz.

Large Tumbling Timber Toy + Dice + Carry/Storage Bag - 54-Pc Wooden Blocks - Premium Pine Wood Floor Game for Kids & Adults - Grows from 1.5-feet to Almost 3-feet While Playing, Life Size Tower While many games make the claim that they are suitable for the whole family - this one is actually FUN for the whole family!

As most are familiar with the game Jenga, this is essentially played the same way - pull a block from the stack and place it on top. If your block causes the tower to tumble, you lose. The primary difference is the blocks are SUPERSIZED, measuring 7.1”(long) X 2.3”(wide) X 1.4”(tall). The blocks are the perfect size for little hands and kids get the hang of the game quickly and enjoy seeing the tower grow and eventually topple.

While the game’s tower begins at around 2’ it quickly grows to 4-5’+. The blocks are not only bigger but they are made of high grade pine, sanded smooth - 20 of the blocks are numbered (1-8, some numbers are duplicated while others are not) allowing players to develop a limitless number of custom games. Something we do is let the winner of each game write their name, or a short message on a block - it makes it fun to look back and remember the fun we have had during previews games.

In addition to the blocks this set comes complete with a wooden crate for storage and travel that easily doubles as a stable, flat playing surface when needed. In addition there is a white board with a dry erase marker for listing the rules you’ve set for the numbered blocks. Due to the 8 block being a one of a kind, we call it the Magic 8 Block and use that as a wild card type block - the person who pulls and places it can name whatever rule they choose.

This is a game reminiscent of games of old - no batteries, nothing electronic, it will last forever, can go anywhere to be played inside or out and is loads of fun for everyone.

This is most definitely a game set I recommend. We have loved it!
text_fidelity_b: Large Tumbling Timber Toy + Dice + Carry/Storage Bag - 54-Pc Wooden Blocks - Premium Pine Wood Floor Game for Kids & Adults - Grows from 1.5-feet to Almost 3-feet While Playing, Life Size Tower

Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games From the first time I saw Fallout the board game on the shelf I knew I wanted it. I have been a fan of the Fallout line since the first game. I have play almost every Fallout video game to come out and it was time to get the board game. After watching a couple videos on how to play, I was very intimidated. There seemed to be a lot of moving parts, card decks and miniatures. My fiancé and I play a most of our games together and I was thinking this would be one that would be a little out of her comfort zone.

I played through the single player game mode and enjoyed the game from the start. After the first game I knew the game was not as complicated as I thought. The game was so fun I stayed up till 3 am playing the game another 2 times. The next day I set it up for my fiancé and I, and I wasn’t disappointed. My favorite part of the game is the questing. The flavor and the ways you go about completing the quest feel like playing a video game. This is the closet I have come, in a board game, to a video game RPG. With hundreds of quest cards, the game replay is awesome. We both enjoyed the game and can’t wait to introduce it to our play group.

I play a lot of tabletop games with miniature and the piece in Fallout are top quality. Before long they will be painted and looking great on the great design of the game tiles. It really feels like you are in the wastelands. For those of you that have played the games, look forward to the quest for the Wasteland Survival Guide! All of the cards are well designed and I really like the decks are different physical sizes. There wasn’t enough room in the box for the insert and all the cards/game pieces. And there was not enough bags for all the game pieces, packaging could have been thought out a little more. Other than that, the game is great and I am looking forward to the expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

The drum barrel has handles on each side for easy lifting (though everything is very light). The lid has ten large bells on it, and it can be removed from the drum and used as a tambourine. Stored inside are two snakes (drumsticks), two giraffes (maracas/rattles), a hornbill (water whistle--you fill with water in the hole in the head, then blow on the whistle for a warble sound), an antelope (slide whistle--you blow in the whistle while sliding the legs in and out to change the tone), and a crocodile (cabasa-clacker--you rotate the handle to make the drum play itself).

It's supposed to be for ages 2-6. My just-turned-1-year-old niece loves playing with this, and so do the adults. The only thing my niece couldn't figure out yet were the whistles. (The water whistle requires just the right amount of water and blowing angle to warble, otherwise it'll do a high pitched whistle.) Our house has become full of joyful noise. lol. Anyway, this set looks fairly sturdy and has been holding up to play just fine so far, but it's clearly a kids-level quality in terms of the sound.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B. Jungle Jam - Toy Drum Set (Includes 9 Percussion Instruments for Kids) (BX1289Z)

Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults When I was in middle school, a teacher I did not really know invited me in to learn chess. It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.

From the moment I pulled her out of the Amazon box, she has been my youngest new favorite thing. It's been a couple of weeks now and my daughter still carries her around the house all day long. I was worried some of the features would get "old" and then soon we just have another doll to add to the toy pile. Lucky, that hasn't happened the thrill hasn't worn off. It just feels like a step up from the first round of baby doll to me. But even then, I bet kids who aren't into swaddling and carrying around newborn baby dolls, would still love this because of the interactive features. And even cut my older preteen boys playing with it, so kids of any age do enjoy it!

Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary [[VIDEOID:e1253051a67b2634f9e78ac021248ab6]] I will be the first person to admit that I purchased these because I always wanted Sea Monkeys as a kid but for some reason I never got them.

The video was shot on day 5 after I put the eggs in. There are quite a few little guys swimming around it the water and they are doing fantastic. I used spring water in their tank, kept my hands and fingers OUT of the tank and placed them in a sunny window during the day and I don't move the tank around much at all. I also aerate them for about 20 seconds every other day with a small air pump and stone that is made for fishbowls, the smallest one you can find.

Mine hatched the day after I put the eggs in.

When the kit arrived, I rinsed it out with the spring water after taking everything out of it. Then I filled it to the fill line with spring water, put the lid on it and let it sit for 24 hours.

The next day, I poured the water purifier in. I didn't stir it, I didn't mess with it at all. I poured the pack in and then put the lid back on the tank.

Next day I aerated the water then poured in the eggs. Again, no stirring or anything. I left it alone, put the lid back on and walked away.

The next day, low and behold I had teeny tiny babies swimming around.

Fed them on the 5th day after they hatched, which was a few hours before I took that video footage.

I'll update again when they are larger but so far I'm really getting a kick out of this. It would appear that the secret is less is more, spring water, don't move the tank around and a lot of patience.
text_fidelity_b: Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary

Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor

T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set This is a great set to introduce kids (as well as adults) to the art of latch hooking. The instruction book is colorful and easy to follow, with clear directions and beautiful graphics. I would give this a five-star review except for two things:

The book gets you and your child excited to start making beautiful projects (including your own customized designs), yet it provides only enough yarn and canvas to make ONE double-sided, child-size pillow. If you want to make bigger and more complicated projects, you have to order more supplies. Because of this, I felt this was more of a "sample" kit, aimed at giving newcomers a "taste" of latch hooking to get you "hooked." For $30, I expected enough material to make at least two projects. Also, what yarn there is of so-so quality - it's rather light and thin, "play yarn" for children, I guess.

Also the packaging felt odd. The book is tied to an empty cardboard box that seems to have no function other than to fill space to make the kit look bigger and more substantial than it is. It's tied so tightly with pipe cleaners that you can't help but tear the back of the book as you try to free it. Another reviewer commented that this may be due to craft stores experiencing a lot of shoplifting - but the book could have been easily secured using double sided tape or light adhesive.

Other than that, this kit will provide hours of enjoyment for adults and kids, especially those (like me) suffering from cabin fever thanks to an interminably long winter. I would definitely buy more as gifts if it were less than the current price.
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set
